issues.headline: The first issue: what inspired me this month
issues.intro:
Welcome to the first issue of The Almanac, a monthly note where I'll share what inspired me to create, new drops, deals, and what's coming next.

First, a quick introduction. Hi, I'm the maker behind Grimoire Glam, and I have been loving this creative outlet.

I came up with the idea after quitting a job of five years to do something that would help me climb out of the rut I had dug for myself. I have always loved getting my nails done, and they have always been a part of my identity. But I never had the creativity or the patience to do what nail techs do, and I still don't. I'm in awe of the fine art they create. This was my way into a creative headspace where my imagination could wander.

Hopefully this goes great! Let's get into the first issue.

stories.title: My new logo
stories.text:
This was a very creative month in the logo department. My old logo was my attempt to make a hand, and it was pretty much missing the target.

I was scrolling aimlessly on Pinterest (as one does) when I saw a photo and was immediately inspired. It sparked a nostalgic idea from one of my favorite shows, Lizzie McGuire. I loved how her animated character expressed her inner thoughts and how she truly felt on the inside. When I saw this caricature I related right away and felt a real connection, so I decided to use it as inspiration for my logo.

I knew it needed to show my deep rooted Latina attitude while still being relatable. I gave her green hair like mine, long dark hair, big eyes, and no waist in sight (haha).

I also ended up learning some new Procreate skills and how to use the program better, which carried into the majority of my new products for this next month.

I absolutely love when something I come across sticks with me and turns into an idea. That's the spark of inspiration, and when you trust that spark, it can create such a great product.

stories.title: "Pearl"
stories.text:
I recently watched this movie (I know, late to the game), but I always love an amazing story with a COMPLEX female lead. I also loved the aesthetic of the movie: the colors, the camera angles, the outfits, and of course the acting. I was so inspired that I decided to do a nail set, and let me tell you, it looks a lot more complicated than it was.

First I wrote down my concept: a set of pearl nails with huge gems and charms that capture the essence of the movie. Once I had that figured out, I rewatched it to see what stood out to me. The title font. Her favorite pitchfork. The overall cuteness that let Pearl deceive so many of her victims. The dead pig that DIDN'T bother her, even with all the maggots. Her iconic blue bow and ONE of her weapons of choice, the axe. And my personal favorite charm of all, Miss Theda, her TRUE partner in crime. I had to do her justice and capture her "let me eat them" vibes, swimming in the blue lake.

I honestly loved this movie, and I truly appreciate such a complex female character in a story like this. Even though Pearl was complex as fuck... well, that's pretty much it. She was just a messed up character. And I freaking loved it.

I also loved this set because it pushed my creativity and 3D modeling skills to the next level. I was able to take a 2D drawing and turn it into 3D nails and nail art. I am honestly really PROUD of this set.

stories.title: "Unethical" by Faouzia
stories.text:
This song has been EVERYWHERE on my For You page, and I am NOT complaining. It captures the idea of "if you love it, let it go" and "be true to yourself," and I truly resonated with that, as I'm sure a lot of people can. She loved someone with her whole heart and soul and it still wasn't enough for that person, and she finally realized she needed to do things her own way, with only her soul's support. I loved the colors of her singing onstage, her bleeding heart from the heartache, the crushing of the life she had imagined and the leaving of what she knew to find something better.

Her bleeding heart inspired me to do an anatomically correct heart, bright red, as a callback to her bleeding heart on stage. The roses nod to a possible wedding bouquet, and they're red as the sign of love. Her crying heart eyes show the beauty in the pain and what it truly means to love. The tear marks call back "ripping off my skin, just to let you in," showing the self harm she was willing to go through for what she thought she loved and wanted. And of course the cross shows her sacrifice for a better life.

I love this song so much, and it has been amazing to see so many other artists sing it in their own key and add instruments. It shows how people can connect through art and real human emotion.

This has to be one of my new "feeling" sets.

stories.title: Burgundy and green
stories.text:
I saw this plant on one of my walks around my neighborhood this last month and was IMMEDIATELY in love with its colors. I knew I wanted to use them in my next market drop.

I started with a green base, drew up the flowers, color matched them to what I saw, and used my new UV printer to print the design straight onto the nails.

stories.title: Burgundy is my favorite fall color
stories.text:
I have been so inspired by burgundy this fall. I have always loved animal print, so I thought, why not combine the two into a few nail sets for the upcoming market?

First, a tiger print with a fun champagne cat eye under black, which really helps the pattern POP.

The second was inspired by deer fur, but I wanted it to feel natural and not too much like fur. I love how it also reminds me of wood.

And of course a good tortoiseshell is always a GREAT staple for a fall set. I don't see too many that lean red, and I LOVE red, so I kept it in the burgundy family.

stories.title: Giving my workspace a facelift
stories.text:
This has nothing to do with nails, but it's what else I was inspired to work on as a little side project. I've been experimenting with my desk and wall for a while, trying to decide how I want my space to look and feel.

Since we rent, I'm not really allowed to make permanent changes, but I figured out a faux wallpaper with materials and tools I already had. I found a pattern I liked and turned it into a VERY thin 3D-printed filament panel, then put it up with Command strips. It gives a wallpaper look with no chance of damaging the walls, so I could still have some fun while staying 100% renter friendly.

Next came my monitors. I got them from my husband's extra stash in the office. I don't need super high quality monitors because I mostly use them to 3D model and work on my website and spreadsheets, but I still wanted them to feel like part of the aesthetic. I cut some trim from wood I got at Home Depot and knocked it out in a few days. Put together on my monitors, it turned out so great!

I want to put marble contact paper on the drawers I found on Facebook Marketplace, but that will have to be a different post. It's taking a while, but it already looks amazing. I sit here every day, and I wanted the space to feel cozy and safe, a place where I can express myself through any inspiration I get and have the freedom to create.

stories.title: My first market ever
stories.text:
This was my first market... EVER. I was super nervous and worried, but excited too. I was worried I wasn't going to sell anything. I was scared that people would look at my stuff and think "trash." I was lucky enough to have family and friends come support me, and I'm extremely grateful for that.

Like with any new business, you learn a ton, and this event taught me A TON. I have new products I want to add to help people with their nails, and ideas for other products that would be so fun to make and sell. I also got to figure out the best way to set up my table so it catches the eye of people passing by.

The nerves sometimes got the best of me and I felt sick to my stomach, but it felt so great when people came up and bought what I had MADE, because I put a lot of love and hard work into my designs and products.

My mix and match board at the market

closing.title: This month was full of creativity
closing.text: This month was such a great month for creativity. I was open to receiving inspiration even in the mundane parts of everyday life. It is so easy to be cut off from feeling inspired because life usually feels grey. But if you open yourself up to what the world is trying to give you, you'll find the beauty and inspiration you need for that time.
